summary.title: Software Architecture Guide
summary.one_liner: Martin Fowler's guide defines software architecture as "the important stuff" and links to his site's articles on application, enterprise, and GUI architecture, microservices, serverless, and related patterns.
takeaways: Architecture is about identifying the important parts of a system (Ralph Johnson's view) and keeping them in good condition.
Poor architecture accumulates cruft, which slows feature delivery; good internal quality tends to speed delivery.
Application and enterprise architecture differ in scale: application architecture works within a notional application boundary, enterprise architecture coordinates across many codebases and teams.
The page is an index that links to deeper articles on microservices, serverless, micro frontends, MVC, feature toggles, distributed system patterns, and enterprise architecture roles.
summary.summary: This is an index page on martinfowler.com that gives Fowler's view of software architecture and points to related material on the site. It covers definitions of architecture (including Ralph Johnson's "the important stuff" idea), why architecture matters for internal quality and cruft, and how the concept differs between application and enterprise scales. It then gives short summaries of linked topics such as microservices, serverless, micro frontends, GUI/MVC architectures, feature toggles, distributed system patterns, and enterprise architecture in agile organizations.
